add.text:
Read this numbered, cleaned transcript of the owner talking. Turn it into an outline a reader
takes in at a glance: "tangible, familiar, easy to digest". The owner's words for it: "putting
familiar names, like the headings" on the thing being discussed and on each of its parts.

Output Markdown in EXACTLY this shape:

# <the concrete thing being discussed>
## <a familiar name for one part of it>
- <one point, in the owner's own words> [S#, S#]
  - <a detail or example of that point, only if it needs its own line> [S#]
## <the next part>
- <...> [S#]

Rules:
- The H1 is CONCRETE: a thing a reader could point at — a class, a page, a tab, a tool, a feature
  (the owner's example: "Page class"). Never an abstract category like "AI processes", "Thoughts"
  or "Feedback". If the transcript covers several separate things, name them plainly in the one
  H1 ("Page class and Sidebar") and give each its own H2 or H2s.
- Exactly ONE "#" H1. One "##" H2 per distinct part — never invent one just to have more.
- Each H2 is a FAMILIAR name a reader already knows. If a name already exists for that part (the
  owner's example: "Layout"), use that exact name; otherwise use the owner's own word for it.
- ONE BULLET PER POINT, NOT PER SENTENCE. When several sentences make one point (a claim, its
  reason, "so I like that"), merge them into one bullet, a short line in the owner's own words,
  citing every one of those sentences. Filler that makes no point of its own ("Couple of things.")
  gets no bullet: add its number to the nearest bullet's citation instead.
- AT MOST TWO LEVELS: a bullet, and sub-bullets under it. Never a third level.
- KEEP EVERY POINT. Merging sentences that make the same point is required; dropping a point is
  not allowed. Never turn a hedge ("maybe", "I think", "I guess") into a flat claim.
- Cite EVERY sentence number EXACTLY ONCE, in the one bullet where its main point went — never
  under two headings. Form: [S3, S7], each number individually, never a range like [S6-S9]. Use
  only numbers that appear below.

STYLE of anything the owner will read (the owner's rules):
- It is an OVERVIEW of what was said, in the owner's own key words. Never the whole rant, never a retelling.
- Each point has its answer or action baked in: say what is done, what to do, or what is still open. Do not invent an answer the transcript or the facts do not give; mark such a point open instead.
- Order by dependency and ease: clarifications and quick items first, then what depends on them. If neither applies, keep the owner's order.
- Reuse the same names for the same things every time, so they become familiar, and always name the context (the page, class, module or session) a point belongs to.
- Headings are big: "#" for the one subject, "##" for each part, "###" only when a part truly needs a split. Never "####" or smaller. Every heading starts with one fitting emoji icon.
- Under a heading: short titled lists. A status bullet starts with ✅ (done) or ⬜ (not done) when the status is known; otherwise a plain "-" bullet. Few emoji, never decoration.
- Every card cites the clean-sentence numbers it came from, like [S3, S7], each number individually.
Apply this to the headings and bullets of the outline.

Cleaned transcript:
"""

S2. I don't know if it's the same refinement that's driving the V2.
S3. They need to be the same.
S4. This is what I'm saying.
S5. It's like getting the raw prompt into a refined state is very important.
S6. And that means summarized in an accurate way where we haven't missed any sentences and then condensed.
S7. So I don't necessarily need to see the way that these refined expand those are rendering as it is putting the sentence IDs.
S8. S1, S2, S3 dash, and then it has a summary.
S9. And so when it says open question, how are new tasks actually being created?
S10. When I ask a question, I want that to be upgraded to a little question widget, just like a task is created, just like all the things that we can create during these chat sessions.
S11. A question is one of them.
S12. It should be a little question icon block with the question.
S13. And then when the answer comes in, it can be added to that question.
S14. We definitely need to be able to reference.
S15. So we want the question to be created kind of within the context block that we're working with.
S16. So at any given time, we need to be creating these context blocks.
S17. It's kind of like a chat bubble, but then we can put things into.
S18. But it gets a title and this is part of this refinement process.
S19. And so then, whatever topic I'm talking about, I see on the screen.
S20. And then when I switch topics, I see a new topic appear.
S21. And then when I ask questions, they can either go to the root if they don't apply to a topic, or if it's part of that topic discussion, it goes right into that thing.
S22. I mean, right now we're just talking about dictation, and it's not necessarily as important.
S23. However, getting the flow of these conversation cards working where we can create different cards.
S24. I could see them adapt to my words in real time.
S25. And then frankly, it's about kind of merging my sentences, those clean sentences, into those cards.
S26. So if the question card is one of the sentences, boom, it just, you associate that sentence with that card.
S27. And the question card itself, by the way, I think we need a class question that extends task.
S28. So I don't know if this is the right thing for the dictation mastermind.
S29. We probably want to do a quick past work check because I think I was explaining this yesterday, something about a question class extending task.
S30. The reason why a question can extend task is that a question could have that same completion idea.
S31. Question is not complete until it's been answered.
S32. And so, one, frankly, I kind of feel like my questions should go incomplete until I accept the answer because — not necessarily.
S33. I ask a lot of questions, but generally if I ask a question and I don't ever see the answer, then I need to.
S34. I need to be reminded of it.
S35. Here's the thing that you were looking for.
S36. I need to go through those and kind of try and understand.
S37. If I'm asking a question, it's because I don't understand, and I need to — until I read the answer and I'm satisfied with it, then that question should remain incomplete, in my opinion.
S38. So anyway, maybe launch a secondary agent to build a quick question class.
S39. But we want that to be generalized so that we can create any kind of cards, whether it's a question or a statement or a task or whatever.
S40. We want those.
S41. Well, I'm figuring out how to organize those in the session log.
S42. I was a little confused about this yesterday.
S43. Talk to the mastermind, see what it thinks about the best way to structure the tasks along with the chat.
S44. I think we made a conclusion about that.
S45. Ask the mastermind how chat items are logged alongside tasks, where some messages might not actually be tasks.
S46. Currently, most of the prompts themselves, I think, the prompt extends tasks.
S47. So I think prompts, oh, I think the answer there was that the session only has tasks.
S48. That's kind of its log.
S49. And the prompts themselves are added to the tasks as prompt instances, and then the messages can be added, your responses essentially can be added as messages to the actual prompts.
S50. So, and the way that the prompt is rendered in terms of the chat bubbles and the group, we need to take a solid look at that.
S51. That might be different.
S52. That probably is different between V1 and V2.
S53. We definitely need to unify these concepts.
S54. So, help me understand what a prompt — are we using a prompt class?
S55. Where does that class live?
"""

Output ONLY the Markdown described above (the H1, its H2s, and their bullets), nothing else.
